name: Allocation churn
definition_present: memory is mapped and unmapped (mmap/munmap, brk) hundreds of times per second or more

name: Straggler at a barrier
definition_present: threads that meet at a barrier keep waiting for the same late thread

name: Slowest thread or bottleneck
definition_present: one thread (or one stage) holds up the whole program, which would run at least 25% faster without its delay
how_users_ask: ["why is the program slow?","what's the bottleneck?"]

name: Busy-waiting or spinning
definition_present: a thread uses a full CPU while waiting for something, making no progress

name: Convoy or serialization
definition_present: threads that could run in parallel run one at a time because of a shared lock
how_users_ask: ["the threads run one after another instead of in parallel"]

name: CPU hog or busiest thread
definition_present: one thread keeps a CPU close to 100% busy for most of the run
how_users_ask: ["what's using all the CPU?","which thread is busiest?"]

name: CPU starvation
definition_present: a runnable thread gets (almost) no CPU time for a long stretch (seconds)
how_users_ask: ["it's ready but never gets to run"]

name: Crash or abnormal exit
definition_present: a process of the program dies from a signal (segfault, abort, kill) rather than exiting

name: Deadlock
definition_present: two or more threads each hold a lock the other needs, and stay blocked for good
how_users_ask: ["two things are waiting on each other"]

name: Excessive migrations
definition_present: threads move between CPUs very often (hundreds of times per second)

name: Failing calls in a retry loop
definition_present: the same system call fails over and over (an error return each time)

name: File churn
definition_present: files are created, opened, closed or deleted at a high rate (hundreds per second)

name: Fork or exec storm
definition_present: the program starts short-lived processes at a high rate (tens per second or more)

name: Gradual slowdown
definition_present: iterations get steadily slower from the start of the run to the end, to at least twice their initial length

name: Hang or freeze
definition_present: the program stops making progress for good: its threads stay blocked until the end of the trace

name: Polling with no work
definition_present: a thread repeatedly checks for work or data (poll, select, read with no wait) that is never there

name: Idle thread
definition_present: a thread exists for the whole run but never does any work

name: Idle workers
definition_present: most workers of a pool stay idle while one or a few do all the work
how_users_ask: ["the workers are idle while one works"]

name: Interrupt storm
definition_present: interrupt handling (hardware interrupt handlers) takes a large share of one CPU, 10% or more for seconds at a time, where a CPU normally spends about 1% in them

name: Jitter
definition_present: a periodic activity's lateness or duration varies continuously, by a quarter of its period or more, throughout the run
how_users_ask: ["the timing varies a lot","it's not steady"]

name: Load imbalance
definition_present: work is unevenly divided: some threads of a group get at least twice as much of it as others
how_users_ask: ["one worker does all the work","uneven load"]

name: Lock contention
definition_present: threads block on the same lock many times per second because another thread holds it

name: Lock holder sleeping or doing I/O while holding it
definition_present: a lock is held across a sleep, I/O or a preemption, and other threads wait on it meanwhile

name: Long blocked waits
definition_present: a thread that has work to do is blocked for a quarter or more of its time, or for seconds at a time (not counting idle waits for new work or its own timed sleeps)
how_users_ask: ["it waits a long time","it's blocked a lot"]

name: Too many small calls
definition_present: the program makes tens of thousands of tiny system calls per second where a few large ones would do

name: Memory pressure or page faults
definition_present: the program spends a quarter or more of its time in page faults or memory reclaim

name: Never exits
definition_present: the program has finished its work but its process stays alive until the end of the trace

name: Noisy neighbour
definition_present: another process competes for the program's CPUs and slows its work down by 25% or more

name: One-off delay or missed deadline
definition_present: a single iteration (or a few in one stretch) of an otherwise regular activity takes at least 5x its usual time
how_users_ask: ["it got delayed once","one request took 15 ms"]

name: Oversleeping
definition_present: most sleeps end 1 ms or more later than requested while the CPU is free (late timer expiry, not CPU contention)
how_users_ask: ["the timer fires late","it sleeps longer than asked"]

name: Oversubscription
definition_present: at least twice as many runnable threads as CPUs, so threads queue for the CPU

name: Priority inversion
definition_present: a high-priority thread waits on a lock held by a lower-priority thread, which is itself kept off the CPU by a medium-priority thread
how_users_ask: ["the high-priority task waits on a low-priority one"]

name: Producer and consumer out of step
definition_present: a queue between two threads keeps swinging between full and empty

name: Real-time thread preempted
definition_present: a real-time (SCHED_FIFO/RR) thread is repeatedly preempted by a higher-priority one

name: Slow to get scheduled
definition_present: a runnable thread is kept waiting to run for 1 ms or more at least 50 times in the trace, or for 10 ms or more at least once
how_users_ask: ["it's ready but has to wait for the CPU","scheduling delay"]

name: Slow shutdown
definition_present: the program takes seconds from its last unit of work to its exit

name: Slow start-up
definition_present: the program takes seconds from its start to its first unit of work
how_users_ask: ["it takes long to start doing work"]

name: Slow system calls or I/O
definition_present: a thread spends 10% or more of its time waiting inside system calls (not counting sleeps or waits for events), some of which take milliseconds
how_users_ask: ["which calls are slow?","file access is slow"]

name: Slowest pipeline stage
definition_present: one stage of a pipeline is too slow for its input, and the stages around it wait for it

name: Sudden change
definition_present: iterations are fast up to one point in the run and at least twice as slow from then on (a step)
how_users_ask: ["it was fine, then got slow around 40 s"]

name: Many slow outliers (tail latency)
definition_present: a small share (about 1-5%) of requests or iterations are many times slower than the median, spread over the whole run
how_users_ask: ["some requests are slow","the p99 is bad"]

name: Thread churn
definition_present: the program creates and ends threads at a high rate (tens per second or more)

name: Thread differences
definition_present: one thread of a group of similar threads behaves differently in a way the rest do not share (e.g. at least twice their CPU time, blocking, or system calls of a kind they make none of)
how_users_ask: ["why does worker-2 behave differently from the others?"]

name: Thundering herd
definition_present: each event wakes many waiting threads, and all but one go straight back to sleep
how_users_ask: ["many threads wake up but only one does anything"]

name: Unexpected activity
definition_present: the program does something unrelated to its job (here: reads files that have nothing to do with it)
how_users_ask: ["what is this process doing?","why is it touching that file?"]

name: Waiting on disk
definition_present: a thread spends a quarter or more of its time blocked on storage I/O (writes, syncs, reads)

name: Waiting on network
definition_present: a thread spends a quarter or more of its time blocked on network communication with another machine

name: Waiting on another process
definition_present: threads spend a quarter or more of their time blocked waiting for replies from another process
how_users_ask: ["it's waiting on the database or the other service"]
